title: Sandhi प्रकरणम् — A Comprehensive Sandhi Rule Book
subtitle: Compiled with reference to Swamini Svatmabodhananda Saraswati's 'सन्धिः' (Sanskrit Grammar Series-3), cross-referenced to पाणिनि's अष्टाध्यायी and the लघुसिद्धान्तकौमुदी of वरदराज
source_note: Rule topics, ordering, and pedagogical examples follow the structure of the source manual 'सन्धिः – Euphonics in Sanskrit' by Swamini Svatmabodhananda Saraswati (Arsha Avinash Foundation, 2017), a teaching manual for Samskrita Bharati अक्ष्हरम् students. That manual states rules descriptively without सूत्र citations; the अष्टाध्यायी सूत्र and लघुसिद्धान्तकौमुदी (LSK) references in this JSON have been added independently as the standard, traditionally-accepted mappings, and examples have been independently composed/verified rather than copied verbatim from the source.

how_to_read.lsk_prakarana: The traditional section (प्रकरण) of the लघुसिद्धान्तकौमुदी of वरदराज in which the rule is treated: Ac-sandhi (vowel sandhi), Hal-sandhi (consonant sandhi), or Visarga-sandhi

svara_sandhi.rule: When two similar (सवर्ण) simple vowels — short or long, of the same class (अ/आ, इ/ई, उ/ऊ, ऋ/ॠ, ऌ) — come together, they are replaced by a single long vowel of that class.
svara_sandhi.lsk_prakarana: Ac-sandhi प्रकरण (लघुसिद्धान्तकौमुदी, सूत्र 26 in the standard ac-sandhi sequence, following एकः पूर्वपरयोः)

svara_sandhi.rule: When अ or आ is followed by a dissimilar simple vowel इ/ई, उ/ऊ, or ऋ/ॠ, the two are together replaced by the corresponding गुण letter: ए (for इ/ई), ओ (for उ/ऊ), अर् (for ऋ/ॠ).
related_ashtadhyayi: 1.1.2 (अदेङ् गुणः — definition of गुण as अ, ए, ओ)
1.1.51 (उरण् रपरः — ऋ replaced by गुण gets a following र्)
svara_sandhi.lsk_prakarana: Ac-sandhi प्रकरण (follows एकः पूर्वपरयोः; precedes वृद्धिर् eci)

svara_sandhi.rule: When अ or आ is followed by ए or ओ (गुण) or ऐ or औ (वृद्धि), the two are replaced by the corresponding वृद्धि letter: ऐ (for ए/ऐ), औ (for ओ/औ).
related_ashtadhyayi: 1.1.1 (वृद्धिर् आदैच् — definition of वृद्धि as आ, ऐ, औ)

svara_sandhi.rule: When a short or long इ, उ, ऋ, or ऌ (ik) is followed by any dissimilar vowel, it is replaced by the corresponding semivowel: य् (for इ/ई), व् (for उ/ऊ), र् (for ऋ/ॠ), ल् (for ऌ).
svara_sandhi.lsk_prakarana: Ac-sandhi प्रकरण (opening rule of ac-sandhi, LSK सूत्र 17)

svara_sandhi.english_name: Substitution of ec vowels by ay/av/आय्/आव्
svara_sandhi.rule: When ए, ओ, ऐ, or औ (the ec vowels) are followed by any vowel, they are respectively replaced by अय्, अव्, आय्, आव्.
svara_sandhi.lsk_prakarana: Ac-sandhi प्रकरण (LSK सूत्र 19, immediately following iko यणचि)

svara_sandhi.rule: When a pada-final ए or ओ is followed by अ, that अ is optionally elided (avagraha ऽ marks the elision) and the preceding ए/ओ alone remains — i.e. the preceding form (पूर्वरूप) is retained as the single substitute.
svara_sandhi.process: vikalpena आदेशः (optional retention — the option is called पूर्वरूप; when not applied, गुण/other sandhi may occur)

svara_sandhi.rule: When a pada-final ए or ओ (एङ्) is followed by ए (in certain prefix + verb combinations, notably with the augment or with the preposition अव), the following form alone remains as the single substitute.

examples.iast: upa + एन्द्रः pattern (illustrative of एङि पररूपम्)

svara_sandhi.note: This rule is comparatively rare/specialised; the source manual treats it alongside पूर्वरूप as one of the ten types of svarasandhi.

svara_sandhi.english_name: Substitution of final आ/ओ of a root by अव्
svara_sandhi.rule: The finals आ of the root ओ (o) — as in roots ending in ओ such as गो — are replaced by अव् when a vowel-beginning affix follows.

examples.sandhi: गो + अम् = गवाम् (in inflection of गो)

svara_sandhi.note: Included by the source manual among the ten svara-sandhi types; strictly this belongs to अङ्गकार्य (stem-modification before case-affixes) rather than inter-pada sandhi proper, but is retained here to preserve the manual's ten-fold classification.

svara_sandhi.rule: In certain fixed circumstances (e.g. before a pluta vowel, before a प्रगृह्य vowel, in the case of the dual ending long ई/ऊ/ए, or after certain particles), no sandhi change takes place even though two vowels stand in contact — the vowels remain in their original (प्रकृति) form.
related_ashtadhyayi: 6.1.125 (no sandhi for pluta/प्रगृह्य before a vowel)
svara_sandhi.lsk_prakarana: Ac-sandhi प्रकरण (LSK सूत्रस् 29–30, closing the vowel-sandhi section)

examples.sandhi: हरी एतौ (dual, remains unchanged before vowel)
अम्बा इति (no sandhi, particle iti after प्रगृह्य)

vyanjana_sandhi.rule: When स् or a dental (त-वर्ग) consonant is immediately followed by श् or a palatal (च-वर्ग) consonant, the स्/dental is replaced by the corresponding palatal (श् or च-वर्ग letter).
vyanjana_sandhi.lsk_prakarana: Hal-sandhi प्रकरण (LSK सूत्र 31, opening rule of hal-sandhi)

vyanjana_sandhi.rule: When स् or a dental (त-वर्ग) consonant is immediately followed by ष् or a cerebral (ट-वर्ग) consonant, the स्/dental is replaced by the corresponding cerebral (ष् or ट-वर्ग letter).
vyanjana_sandhi.lsk_prakarana: Hal-sandhi प्रकरण (paired with श्चुत्व, LSK सूत्र 31)

vyanjana_sandhi.english_name: Softening of a final hard consonant before a soft/vowel
vyanjana_sandhi.rule: A word-final jhal consonant (hard consonant of any varga, or स्/ह् etc.) is replaced by the third (जश्) letter of its own class when followed by a soft (voiced) consonant or a vowel.
related_ashtadhyayi: 8.4.53 (झलां जश् झशि — जश्त्व also before a soft consonant medially)

examples.iast: षड् + हस्तः = षड्ढस्तः (जश्त्व then further change)

vyanjana_sandhi.english_name: Hardening of a soft consonant before a hard consonant
vyanjana_sandhi.rule: A soft (voiced) consonant at the end of a word is replaced by the corresponding first-letter hard (कठोर) consonant of its class (्, चर्) when a hard (खर्) consonant follows.
related_ashtadhyayi: 8.2.30 (चोः कुः — palatal/cartva to guttural before hard consonant), 8.4.54 (अभ्यासे carc)
vyanjana_sandhi.process: आदेशः (substitution, the reverse process of जश्त्व)

vyanjana_sandhi.english_name: Optional nasalisation of a final consonant before a nasal
vyanjana_sandhi.rule: A word-final consonant belonging to the yar प्रत्याहार (i.e. any consonant except nasals and semivowels), when followed by a nasal (ङ्, ञ्, ण्, न्, म्), may optionally be replaced by the nasal (अनुनासिक) of its own class.

vyanjana_sandhi.english_name: म् becomes अनुस्वार before a consonant
vyanjana_sandhi.rule: A word-final म्, when followed by any consonant (not a vowel), is replaced by अनुस्वार (ं).
related_ashtadhyayi: 8.3.24 (नश् ca अपदान्तस्य jhali — non-final न्/म् also become अनुस्वार before jhal)

vyanjana_sandhi.english_name: अनुस्वार becomes the nasal homogeneous with the following consonant
vyanjana_sandhi.rule: An अनुस्वार, when followed by a consonant belonging to the yay प्रत्याहार (i.e. any consonant except स्/श्/ष्/ह्), is optionally replaced by the nasal (सवर्ण) of that consonant's own class.

vyanjana_sandhi.english_name: Nasal assimilation to the preceding consonant
vyanjana_sandhi.rule: When (except for a nasal itself) a class (वर्गीय) consonant is immediately followed by a nasal of its own class, either consonant may, by convention of some grammarians' teaching order, be treated as assimilating — in the source manual's presentation this covers cases like विपद्वत् type clusters where a following nasal conditions the preceding stop; treated together with cartva/जश्त्व contexts.
vyanjana_sandhi.sutra_iast: See 8.4.58 (अनुस्वारस्य yayi परसवर्णः) for the general परसवर्ण principle applied in both directions
vyanjana_sandhi.note: The source manual lists this as a distinct lesson (no. 7 in its consonant-sandhi list) illustrating वणिक्+hasati / विट्+hasati type forms; it functions as a corollary of जश्त्व + परसवर्ण working together rather than a wholly separate पाणिनिअन् सूत्र.

vyanjana_sandhi.english_name: Optional श् → छ् after certain finals
vyanjana_sandhi.rule: श्, when preceded by a word ending in a short vowel followed by तुक् (त्) augment, or in specific tuk-augment contexts, may optionally be replaced by छ्.
vyanjana_sandhi.ashtadhyayi_ref: 6.1.73 (che ca — tuk augment before छ), cf. 8.4.63
vyanjana_sandhi.note: Presented in the source manual as 'श् optionally changes to छ्' after श्चुत्व has converted a preceding त्/स् to च्; the resulting च् + श् cluster optionally further strengthens to च्छ्.

vyanjana_sandhi.rule: In defined morphological contexts a preceding न् or a visarga-derived स् interacts with a following स्; broadly, forms where a dental nasal or sibilant environment resolves to स् are covered under this heading (e.g. सजुषो रुः — the स् of the word sajus, and general 'sa' as substitute of visarga, are treated in this section by the source manual).

examples.sandhi: रामः + करोति (visarga retained as स् before hard) = रामस्करोति (historical/कारिका form)

vyanjana_sandhi.note: This lesson bridges hal-sandhi and visarga-sandhi in the source manual's ordering, since the स्/रु substitute for visarga is foundational to both.

vyanjana_sandhi.rule: Within the same word, न् is replaced by ण् when preceded (not necessarily immediately, but without intervention of a coronal/palatal/velar obstruent or a pause) by र्, ष्, or the vowel ऋ/ॠ.
vyanjana_sandhi.lsk_prakarana: Hal-sandhi / pada-प्रकरण (LSK सूत्र 135 in the six-genders section, but conceptually part of consonant sandhi)

vyanjana_sandhi.rule: A short vowel standing at the end of a word, when followed by छ्, receives the insertion (आगम) of त् between the vowel and छ्.
related_ashtadhyayi: 6.1.71 (hrasvasya piti कृति tuk — a related tuk-insertion in कृत् formations)
vyanjana_sandhi.lsk_prakarana: Ac-sandhi / Hal-sandhi boundary (LSK सूत्र 39, immediately after ङमुटागम)

vyanjana_sandhi.english_name: Insertion of a homogeneous nasal augment (ङमुट्)
vyanjana_sandhi.rule: When a short vowel at the end of a word is followed by a nasal consonant which is itself followed by a vowel, the intervening nasal-augment (सवर्ण nasal, called ङमुट्) is compulsorily inserted after the short vowel.

examples.iast: illustrative pattern of ङमुट् before nasal+vowel

vyanjana_sandhi.note: This is a relatively technical, less frequently drilled rule; the source manual lists it (Lesson 13) primarily for completeness of the fourteen-rule consonant-sandhi scheme.

vyanjana_sandhi.english_name: त-वर्ग changed to ल् before ल्
vyanjana_sandhi.rule: A dental (त-वर्ग: त्, थ्, द्, ध्, न्) at the end of a word is changed to ल् (with an inserted nasalised ल् for न्) when followed by ल्.
vyanjana_sandhi.ashtadhyayi_ref: 8.4.60 (lo 'ci ca) with 8.4.62/63 context; commonly cited as tor लः in traditional grammar
vyanjana_sandhi.lsk_prakarana: Hal-sandhi प्रकरण (closing rule of the consonant-sandhi lessons in the source manual)

visarga_sandhi.rule: Word-final स् and र् (in the नामपद when not followed by a vowel or voiced consonant that would trigger other sandhi) are replaced by visarga (​ः) at a pause or before a hard consonant.
related_ashtadhyayi: 8.2.66 (ससजुषो रुः — स्/र् become रु, the basis of visarga)
visarga_sandhi.lsk_prakarana: Visarga-sandhi प्रकरण (LSK सूत्रस् 40–41, opening the section)

visarga_sandhi.english_name: Visarga is retained before hard (khar) consonants
visarga_sandhi.rule: When visarga is followed by a hard (खर्) consonant — i.e. क्, ख्, प्, फ् or a surd of any class — it simply remains unchanged (or, before श्/ष्/स्, optionally changes — see Lesson 2).

visarga_sandhi.english_name: Optional change of visarga to श्/ष्/स् before sibilants
visarga_sandhi.rule: Visarga followed by a sibilant (श्, ष्, स्) may optionally be replaced by that same sibilant (assimilation), or may remain unchanged.
visarga_sandhi.ashtadhyayi_ref: 8.3.34 (with 8.3.36–8.3.38 for the optionality before श/ष/sa specifically)

visarga_sandhi.english_name: Compulsory change of visarga to श्/ष्/स् before palatals, cerebrals, dentals
visarga_sandhi.rule: Visarga, when followed by a palatal (च्/छ्) is replaced by श्; when followed by a cerebral (ट्/ठ्) is replaced by ष्; when followed by a dental (त्/थ्) is replaced by स्.

visarga_sandhi.english_name: Change of visarga preceded by अ to उ before soft consonants
visarga_sandhi.rule: When visarga is preceded by the short vowel अ and followed by a soft (voiced) consonant, it is replaced by उ, which then combines with the preceding अ by गुण-sandhi to give ओ.
visarga_sandhi.sutra_iast: ato ror अप्लुताद् aplute; हशि ca
visarga_sandhi.process: आदेशः → then आद्गुणः (two-step: उ-आदेश, then अ+उ=ओ गुण)

visarga_sandhi.english_name: Elision of visarga (preceded by अ) before a vowel other than अ
visarga_sandhi.rule: When visarga is preceded by the short vowel अ and is followed by any vowel OTHER than अ (i.e. इ, ई, उ, ऊ, ऋ, ए, ऐ, ओ, औ), the visarga is simply elided (लोपः) rather than converting to उ/ओ. No vowel-combination (गुण) takes place; the two words merely stand adjacent with a hiatus. This is distinct from the अ + अ case (visarga-4/svara-6 पूर्वरूप pattern), where visarga becomes ओ and the following अ is elided with an avagraha (रामः + अत्र = रामोऽत्र). Traditionally attributed to शाकल्य's view, in which the visarga's substitute (य्-based/rutva) is treated as silent (लोपः) before a dissimilar vowel.
related_ashtadhyayi: 6.1.109 (एङः पदान्ताद् ati — the contrasting अ+अ→ओ पूर्वरूप case)
visarga_sandhi.lsk_prakarana: Visarga-sandhi प्रकरण (companion case to LSK सूत्रस् 43–44, ato ror अप्लुताद् aplute)
visarga_sandhi.note: Added from analysis of Bhagavad गीता 1.1 (धृतराष्ट्र उवाच). This case was previously a gap in the rule book: visarga-4 only addressed अ-preceded visarga before a soft CONSONANT (→ ओ via गुण), and visarga-6 only addressed आ-preceded visarga (→ lopa). Neither covered अ-preceded visarga before a dissimilar VOWEL, which is the very common 'X उवाच' pattern seen throughout the गीता's speaker-tags. This entry fills that gap.

visarga_sandhi.english_name: Change of visarga (preceded by any vowel other than अ/आ) to र् before soft consonants/vowels
visarga_sandhi.rule: When visarga is preceded by any vowel other than अ or आ, and is followed by a soft consonant or a vowel, it is replaced by र् (repha), which then undergoes further sandhi as an ordinary र्.
visarga_sandhi.sutra_iast: ato ror अप्लुताद् aplute (extended to non-a vowels by the general ru-substitution + subsequent हशि/aci context)

visarga_sandhi.english_name: Elision of visarga after long आ
visarga_sandhi.rule: When visarga is preceded by the long vowel आ and is followed by a soft consonant or any vowel, the visarga is dropped (lopa) entirely.
visarga_sandhi.sutra_iast: The elision of ru after आ is covered by the general working of 6.1.114 हशि ca combined with the fact that आ + u would not remain; traditionally stated as 'visarga is lopa after आ'
visarga_sandhi.ashtadhyayi_ref: 6.1.114 (हशि ca), in conjunction with 8.3.19 (लोपः शाकल्यस्य) principle applied to visarga after आ

visarga_sandhi.english_name: Special allophones of visarga before क्/ख् and प्/फ्
visarga_sandhi.rule: Visarga, when followed by क् or ख्, is optionally pronounced as जिह्वामूलीय (a guttural breath sound); when followed by प् or फ्, is optionally pronounced as उपध्मानीय (a labial breath sound). These are allophonic/orthographic variants and do not change the spelling in ordinary practice.
visarga_sandhi.sutra_devanagari: विसर्गस्य कवर्गे परे जिह्वामूलीयः पवर्गे परे उपध्मानीयः
visarga_sandhi.sutra_iast: (traditional statement, based on) कुप्वोः xa-xa (काशिका gloss on 8.3.37)
visarga_sandhi.lsk_prakarana: Visarga-sandhi प्रकरण (final lesson of the section)

examples.sandhi: रामः + करोति (visarga optionally realised as जिह्वामूलीय before क्)
रामः + पठति (visarga optionally realised as उपध्मानीय before प्)

वरदराज. लघुसिद्धान्तकौमुदी (commentary/translation tradition following भट्टोजि दीक्षित's सिद्धान्तकौमुदी).
शास्त्री, विश्वनाथ. प्रारम्भिकपाणिनीयम् / Parama-laghu-सिद्धान्तकौमुदी. Delhi: Motilal Banarsidass, 1991. (used to cross-verify अष्टाध्यायी सूत्र numbering for ac-, hal-, and visarga-sandhi)

changelog.change: Added rule 'visarga-4b' (visarga-लोपः अकारात् असवर्ण-svare) covering elision of an अ-preceded visarga before a dissimilar vowel (e.g. X + उवाच = X उवाच). This was identified as a gap during analysis of Bhagavad गीता 1.1 and sourced from अष्टाध्यायी 8.3.17/8.3.19 (शाकल्य's view), which is outside the manual this rule book was originally compiled from.
